Its central three-coupling is Fault Diagnosis x Distributed Control x Functional Redundancy. This is scaled, non-occupancy, prospective engineering research, not a claim of a roadworthy autonomous supercar. The core hypothesis is falsifiable. Under resource-matched material, energy, time, sensing, operator and computation budgets, a frozen distributed isolation-and-reallocation architecture should improve qualified residual stiffness or essential-service retention without degrading qualified cycle survival, false-clear rate or stop reliability relative to centralized allocation, scheduled replacement and conservative hardwired stopping. Concealed motor derating, open physical latches, shared power-rail faults, sensor drift, network partitions and signed stale messages challenge the claim. A perfectly coordinated controller cannot clear a physically unverified load path. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates examine survival and competing-risk hazards, censoring, redundancy, observability, normalized innovations, sequential detection, interval and Bayesian identification, network connectivity, stale packets, distributed diagnosis, constrained actuator allocation, actual force-and-moment balance, weak-direction stiffness, safe-set barriers, physical stopping time, measured work, correlated uncertainty and conjunctive release. Every plate specifies a mathematical construction, units and validity assumptions, a unique blind refutation and chapter references. Eighty-two chapters and 410 independent single-page investigations progress from physical fault ontology through distributed observability, bounded load redistribution, qualification, hardware-safe authority, lifetime transfer and successor interfaces. Two hundred Research Gates each carry a specific challenge, an alternative account and a refusal condition. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose instruments, fixtures, protocols and evidence objects with their own failure modes; none is a claim of a completed full-scale nanorobotic vehicle system. This hypothesis-forming edition distinguishes author-supplied F13 evidence ancestry (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839; author-supplied metadata) from externally published methods: decentralized sensor faults (10.1109/TAC.2014.2384371; 10.1109/TCNS.2014.2367362), event-triggered fault isolation (10.1109/TCYB.2023.3344775), resilient multiagent control (10.1109/TCYB.2021.3132380) and intermittent-communication fault tolerance (10.1109/JSYST.2025.3624911).
